function.boundary_source: Exact exported entry + PE x64 exception directory BeginAddress/EndAddress

presentation_regions.label: Grapple anchor
presentation_regions.explanation: Read Plate A and commit the anchor state. The first region also contains real pointer setup and linked stack-probe calls.

presentation_regions.label: Relay power
presentation_regions.explanation: Read switchB and commit relay power.

presentation_regions.label: Lift field
presentation_regions.explanation: Short-circuit plateB OR switchC. These two tests and their output alternatives are separate native regions.

presentation_regions.label: Upper latch / service landing
presentation_regions.explanation: Read the room-owned latch and commit service state. The enabled block also tests payload; the disabled block also clears platform B and exit.

presentation_regions.label: Payload route and exit
presentation_regions.explanation: Latch context plus cube payload test and paired output stores. Shares real blocks with the service region; never fabricate a separate exit decision.

presentation_regions.label: Bridge remains disabled
presentation_regions.explanation: Unconditional zero store followed by return. UPLINK has no enabled bridge requirement.

proof_evidence.quantification: For every independently loaded pair x,y in 0..2^32-1 at each guard; no x=y=0 assumption.
assumptions: Normal entry through uplink_controller and decoded direct control flow; no external jump into an interior instruction or clone.
Code bytes and normal x86-64 instruction semantics remain intact; no debugger/exception mechanism rewrites RIP or flags.
The two 32-bit global loads complete successfully; each loaded x and y may be arbitrary and may differ between guards.
Calls use their ordinary ABI and return to their call sites; no stack/control-flow corruption or return-address manipulation.
This establishes clone unreachability under those conditions, not whole-program equivalence for arbitrary inputs/pointers or hardware faults.

solver.counterexample_formula:
(let ((a!1 (= (bvand (bvmul loaded_x (bvsub loaded_x #x00000001)) #x00000001)
              #x00000000))
      (a!2 (distinct (= ((_ extract 31 31) (bvsub loaded_y #x0000000a)) #b1)
                     (= ((_ extract 31 31) loaded_y) #b1))))
(let ((a!3 (and (distinct (= ((_ extract 31 31) loaded_y) #b1)
                          (= ((_ extract 31 31) #x0000000a) #b1))
                a!2)))
(let ((a!4 (distinct (= ((_ extract 31 31) (bvsub loaded_y #x0000000a)) #b1)
                     a!3)))
(let ((a!5 (= (bvand (bvor (ite a!1 #x01 #x00) (ite a!4 #x01 #x00)) #x01) #x00)))
  (not (not a!5))))))

integration.animation: May separately replay one complete retained trace for each input snapshot; replace/cancel the prior cursor on input change.
integration.layout: Hand-authored frontend geometry and physics; no coordinates in this bundle.

limitations: This validates the 32 canonical Boolean snapshots, including physically unusual states, not arbitrary pointer/value inputs.
Trace events are sequential writes; ControllerFrame.outputs is the completed frame, not a partially initialized struct.
Service and payload regions share actual native blocks; a single decision can commit multiple outputs.
Two actual linked __chkstk calls execute per BCF trace; helper steps are retained and not assigned fake controller blocks.
Current UPLINK has no crumble-prototype object; RELAY has one. Bogus imagery is a future frontend choice, not a binary-owned effect.
No string encryption or decoded messages; current text remains authored mock presentation.
Coverage alone never classifies a block as bogus; clone labels and native predicate proof are required.
